decisions.reason: As a recently launched plugin closely related to pricing communication, it is likely kept because it supports the firm's digital service offering with relatively low ongoing cost.

The ERP interface plugin is somewhat farther from the firm's core marketing focus and can be maintenance-heavy, but it still strengthens integration value for clients so management would likely keep it for now.
Price comparison tracking fits the firm's market-monitoring profile, so a newly launched version would usually be retained while customer uptake is still developing.
With several very similar price comparison tracking plugins launched at the same time, management would likely rationalize overlap and discontinue one of the less differentiated variants.
This product appears redundant within a crowded set of similar tracking plugins, making it a likely candidate to remove so resources can be concentrated on stronger offerings.
Net price reporting is adjacent to the firm's analytics-oriented business and likely complements existing client reporting services, so it would usually remain on the market.
